column1: # THE ADOPTION PROFILE. A filled-in answer sheet for a team that is NOT us.
# WHY TSV AND NOT YAML.
#   1. It is what this repo already uses for every machine-readable declaration
#      -- environments.tsv, ports.tsv, change/label-owners.tsv -- and each of
#      those carries its reasoning in `#` comments beside the rows. A profile is
#      the same kind of object: a small, flat, human-audited declaration whose
#      comments are half the point.
#   2. adopt/generate.sh is POSIX sh and reads this with `while read key value`.
#      A YAML profile would need a parser, which means python3 or a vendored
#      library, which means the generator acquires a dependency that the thing
#      it generates does not have. The generator must run wherever the pipeline
#      it emits will run.
#   3. The key space is deliberately FLAT. Nesting invites a structure where a
#      missing branch and an empty branch look alike, which is the shape of
#      spec.org defect class 8 -- `cannot say` is not `no`. Here a missing key
#      is a missing ANSWER, and generate.sh refuses the whole profile rather
#      than defaulting it. There is no default that is safe for all sixteen
#      questions and pretending otherwise is how a guard gets emitted that
#      nobody chose.
# Two columns, tab-separated: key<TAB>value. Blank lines and `#` lines ignored.
# Every key in adopt/PROFILE.org must be present. Unknown keys are an error.
# THE TEAM. Hypothetical, and deliberately unlike this estate.
# "Wrenbury" is three engineers shipping one Django application to two VMs
# behind a load balancer at a European host. Self-hosted GitLab, one runner on
# the same private network as the VMs. Two environments. No blue/green -- a
# deploy replaces the running process on each VM in turn. They merge to `main`
# and deploy `main`, which is what almost everyone does and which costs them
# three of the controls below.
# They answer NO to five things, and the refusals generate.sh produces for them
# are the reason this file exists. A conformance instrument that only
# demonstrates success has not been shown to reject anything.
profile.name
profile.date
# They wrote a failing fixture for each of their four gates before wiring any
# of this up, because generate.sh emits nothing without it. Two of the four
# fixtures did not fail on the first attempt.
gates.selftest
# --- Section B: what a change is, and what it ships ------------------------
change.unit
change.state.owner
deploy.unit
deploy.unit.derivable
# THE ANSWER THAT COSTS THEM THE MOST, and they did not know it was a question.
# They merge and then deploy `main`. So there is no branch head to compare
# against the trunk: guard 0 has no content, and guard 6 -- do not merge onto a
# trunk production is not serving -- is inverted by construction, because the
# merge is what produces the thing to deploy.
deploy.source
# --- Section C: what the platform can tell you -----------------------------
# Pipelines are per-commit and the runner can reach the VMs over WireGuard, so
# the gates report as real check verdicts rather than as carried records. That
# is the simpler half of the model and they should keep it.
forge.verdicts.per_commit
forge.verdicts.revocable
forge.trunk_moved_event
forge.approver_distinct
forge.reaches_estate
# --- Section D: the shape of the path to production ------------------------
path.environments
path.authorizing
# One team, one application, one path. Nothing contends for it, so a berth
# would be the queue paying for a safety production does not gain -- which is
# spec.org's own test for ceremony. Refused, and correctly.
path.shared
path.lease
# gunicorn is fronted by their own middleware, which sets X-Build-Sha from the
# release file. Two VMs means a mixed fleet is observable, so UNCONVERGED is a
# state guard 5 can actually report.
production.observable
production.build_id
production.replicas
# No idle colour to switch to. Rolling back means deploying the previous tag,
# which takes as long as deploying anything else -- so guard 5's failure path
# is a refusal naming a SHA for a person to restore, not an automatic action.
production.rollback
# Two VMs, two hostnames, each with its own :443. Ports are not scarce, so the
# 9000/9100/9200 tier model buys them nothing at all.
address.namespace.shared
# --- Section E: who may say the estate is closed ---------------------------
# A tracked file on `main` with a CODEOWNERS rule on its path. Not on a change
# -- a freeze recorded on a change exempts its own carrier.
freeze.holder
freeze.declarer
emergency.declarer
# No change schedule. Deploys happen when someone is at a desk. They lose the
# forfeit record and nothing else, because the guards do not read a calendar.
schedule.store
# Not yet declared. generate.sh emits a starter declaration with one row per
# fact it creates, and refuses to emit any control writing a fact it cannot
# name an owner for.
facts.ownership_declared
